criterion: M3 materials (dated addition, 2026-10-10): the glTF 2.0 material model and its ratified material extensions as a float64 CPU reference, with energy, reciprocity and GPU-parity checks
written: 2026-10-10, before the first run and before the implementation was written

model.base: GGX distribution (Trowbridge-Reitz) written with sin^2 = hx^2 + hy^2 so float32 has no cancellation near the peak; height-correlated Smith visibility (anisotropic form, Heitz 2014); Schlick Fresnel with f0 and f90; alpha = roughness^2, roughness clamped to at least 0.045 (Filament's floor for float32).
model.energy: Kulla-Conty multiple scattering with coloured Fresnel, built from tabulated split albedos A(mu, r) and B(mu, r) (F = f0 A + f90 B for Schlick), E = A + B. Under anisotropy the tables are read at the roughness projected on each direction's azimuth, and the normaliser is the azimuthal mean of E_avg.
model.dielectric: Specular layer with f0 = min(((ior-1)/(ior+1))^2 * specularColor, 1) * specular, f90 = specular (KHR_materials_ior, KHR_materials_specular). The base below is weighted by (1 - E_s(mu_o))(1 - E_s(mu_i)) / (1 - E_s_avg), so a white Lambertian base under it conserves energy exactly and the product is reciprocal.
model.clearcoat: An isotropic GGX layer with f0 0.04 and its own normal; the layers below are weighted by (1 - c E_c(mu_o))(1 - c E_c(mu_i)): reciprocal and conservative, losing the energy that would bounce between coat and base.
model.sheen: Charlie distribution (Estevez and Kulla 2017) with the Neubelt visibility (as Filament's cloth); the layers below are weighted by min(1 - s E_sh(mu_o), 1 - s E_sh(mu_i)) as KHR_materials_sheen states, s = max component of the sheen colour.
model.transmission: Thin-walled (no KHR_materials_volume): the specular lobe mirrored through the surface, weighted by min(1 - E_s(mu_o), 1 - E_s(|mu_i|)). With volume: the rough dielectric interface BTDF (Walter et al. 2007) with Schlick at the outside cosine, and Beer-Lambert attenuation over the thickness.
model.iridescence: The Belcour-Barla 2017 thin-film Fresnel as KHR_materials_iridescence writes it, mixed into F by the iridescence factor.

furnace_metal.what: white metal (base colour 1, metallic 1), isotropic, roughness 0.05 to 1.00 by 0.05, mu_o 0.05 to 1.00 by 0.05, integrated through the full material evaluation by Gauss-Legendre quadrature (specular lobe over the half vector, smooth terms over the incident direction)

furnace_dielectric.what: white Lambertian base under the dielectric specular layer, ior 1.33, 1.5 and 2.0, specular 1, same roughness and mu_o grid

furnace_anisotropic.what: white metal with anisotropy 0.3, 0.6 and 1.0, roughness 0.2 to 1.0 by 0.2, mu_o 0.1 to 1.0 by 0.1, view azimuth 0, 45 and 90 degrees from the anisotropy direction
furnace_anisotropic.bound: |albedo - 1| <= 2e-2 (the compensation reads the isotropic tables at the projected roughness, an approximation; the measured value is recorded)

conservation.what: albedo over both hemispheres for white inputs in every family: clearcoat (factor 0.5 and 1, coat roughness 0.05 to 1), sheen (colour 1, sheen roughness 0.1 to 1) over white metal and white dielectric, thin-walled transmission 0.5 and 1, volume transmission with ior 1.5, iridescent metal (thickness 100 to 1000 nm)
conservation.bound: albedo <= 1 + 1e-3 at every point; iridescent dielectric albedo <= 1 + 2e-2 (its base weighting uses the iridescent Fresnel at mu, not at the half vector)

interface_total.what: rough dielectric interface alone (reflection plus Walter transmission, ior 1.5) at roughness 0.05
interface_total.bound: R + T >= 0.99 for mu_o >= 0.2 (checks the refraction Jacobian; the loss to masking is small at low roughness)

reciprocity.what: 20,000 seeded random (material, wo, wi) triples over every family
reciprocity.bound: |f(o,i) - f(i,o)| <= 1e-12 * max(1, |f|) for reflection; for the volume BTDF |f(o,i) / eta_o^2 - f(i,o) / eta_i^2| <= 1e-12 * max(1, |f|) (generalized reciprocity)

clearcoat_zero.what: clearcoat factor 0 against the same material without the extension

iridescence_spectral.what: the Belcour-Barla fast path against a float64 spectral Airy summation with the same Schlick interface reflectances and phase conventions, 380 to 780 nm in 1 nm steps, CIE 1931 colour matching functions from the Wyman, Sloan and Shirley 2013 multi-lobe fit, mapped to linear Rec.709 and normalised so a constant spectrum stays grey; film ior 1.2 to 2.0, thickness 100 to 1000 nm, base ior 1.5 and a gold-like F0, cos theta 0.1 to 1
iridescence_spectral.bound: max |difference| per channel <= 0.05; the measured value is recorded

gpu_parity.what: a WGSL compute pass evaluates f * cos(theta_i) and the emission for a seeded set of 4,096 (material, wo, wi) cases over every family, in float32, reading float32 copies of the same tables; compared with the float64 reference on D3D12 WARP and on WebGPU (SwiftShader in Chrome)
gpu_parity.bound: |gpu - ref| <= 1e-3 * |ref| + 1e-5 for every channel of every case

gpu_control.what: the same comparison with the GPU pass told to drop the multiple-scattering term
gpu_control.bound: fails the parity bound on at least one case

does_not_prove: That the model matches measured materials, or any other engine's look; that texture fetches, normal mapping or tangent frames are right (those belong to the scene renderer); behaviour below the roughness floor (a perfect mirror); that an RTX-class GPU with approximate transcendental instructions meets the parity bound (measured separately under the GPU lock).
